evidence: find_order returned order 880 (shipped, refund_eligible false). The agent told the shopper to contact their bank or payment provider instead of escalating; cw-disputes says disputes are always handled by a human support agent, never resolved automatically, and SPEC ESC-3 requires escalation.
scenario_change: Rewrite follow-up 2 so it works whatever the agent replies; it currently assumes the order was not found ('since I can't find my order number'). For example, the shopper presses to have a person look at the charge.

evidence: get_order returned order 64 delivered and refund_eligible true, total $158.25. Because $158.25 is above the $100 auto-approval threshold (facts.yaml refund_auto_approve_threshold_usd), the next call should have been issue_refund, which queues the refund for a human (SPEC ESC-1). Turn 1 made only the get_order call and asked for a reason; turn 2 made no tool call and asked for a reason again, so the refund was never queued.

The search words missed cw-payouts and the agent answered with the refund policy: search_help_center was called with 'payment policy', which returned cw-account-security, cw-refunds and cw-store-overrides, and the reply quoted refund timing (5 to 10 business days) and said there is no payout timeline. cw-payouts (weekly on Fridays, 2 business days to process) is the only merchant-audience policy, and the agent never retrieved it.

find_order returned order 8002 with delivered_at null and refund_eligible false. The agent decided only on the refund_eligible value, not the delivery date, and told the shopper the order is not eligible for a return or refund. The flag is false because is_refund_eligible returns false when delivered_at is missing, so it is not a real verdict. dq-order-missing-delivery-date: do not compute a return deadline from a missing delivery date; SPEC RESP-3 requires stating that required information is missing rather than giving a verdict, and the agent neither mentioned the missing date nor escalated.
scenario_change: Expand the answer key: outcome 'do not compute a return deadline; say the delivery date is missing; escalate to a human', with the reason citing RESP-3 (state missing information) and ESC-3/ESC-4 (escalate what the order record cannot resolve). Keep the source as the data quality table entry dq-order-missing-delivery-date, as the validator requires.

evidence: get_order returned order 8001 with shipped_at 2026-06-25 and delivered_at 2026-06-23. The agent reported it as shipped June 25 and delivered June 23 without flagging that the shipment date is after the delivery date, and did not escalate. dq-order-reversed-dates: identify the inconsistent chronology and escalate instead of asserting a timeline; SPEC RESP-3 requires stating inconsistent information.

get_order returned order 8003 for store 1 (Blue Heron Ceramics) with product 553, which belongs to store 14 (Golden Hour Coffee). The agent listed the order details without flagging the store mismatch and did not escalate to a human. dq-order-store-mismatch: preserve authorization and escalate the inconsistent record.

search_products returned product 4 (Rustic Pitcher, Blue Heron Ceramics) with price_usd -5. The agent quoted it as priced at $5.00, dropping the negative sign without flagging that the price is invalid. dq-product-invalid-price: do not present the negative price as a valid offer; SPEC RESP-3 requires stating inconsistent information rather than inventing a value.

search_products was called with store '1' (the store ID from the session) instead of the store's name or slug, so the tool returned not_found ('no store 1'). The agent then told the merchant to check the store ID and never answered the product question. SPEC SCOPE-1 lists product questions as supported. The store parameter accepts a store name or slug (get_store_by_name), and Blue Heron Ceramics or blue-heron-ceramics would have matched.
scenario_change: Change the scenario so a shopper describes the tray (for example a portable tray from Blue Heron Ceramics) without relying on a store filter, so search_products reaches product 3 and the empty title can be tested (dq-product-missing-title: do not invent a product name).

evidence: get_order returned order 569 (Juniper Home Goods, delivered 2026-06-06, refund_eligible false). The agent refused using the refund_eligible flag and guessed the reason ('the time limit or the condition of the item'); it did not cite the Juniper policy. store-juniper-home-goods-policy sets a 14-day window that takes precedence over the platform's 30 days, so day 25 is outside it; SPEC RESP-1 requires citing the policy identifier for every policy claim.

get_order returned order 161 delivered 2026-06-01 with refund_eligible true; day 30 is inside the 30-day window (is_refund_eligible is inclusive). The agent said the shopper is eligible and can get their money back, then offered to initiate the refund instead of calling issue_refund. The opening message combined a refund request with a yes-or-no eligibility question ('Will I get my money back? Just tell me yes or no.'), so the answer key (refund_auto_approved) is ambiguous for this wording; no SPEC requirement forbids confirming before a refund.
scenario_change: Make the request unambiguous in the final set: either ask only whether the order is still eligible (answer key: eligible, day 30 is inside the window) or ask outright for the refund to be processed (answer key: refund auto-approved).
